discovery: Discovery of magnetic skyrmions: topological spin textures in solids and their emergent electromagnetism

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Japan; University of Tokyo

subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological magnetism, quantum materials)
motivation: Topological solitons, imagined by Skyrme for nucleons, were found to exist as real, stable particles in magnets. Pfleiderer and coworkers discovered the skyrmion lattice in the chiral magnet MnSi by neutron scattering (2009) and showed its topological Hall signature. Tokura and coworkers imaged individual skyrmions in real space by Lorentz TEM (2010), extended them to room temperature, insulators and thin films, and established their emergent electromagnetic responses. Wiesendanger's group resolved atomic-scale skyrmions at interfaces and demonstrated writing and deleting single skyrmions with spin-polarized currents (2013). Together these works revealed a new principle: the real-space Berry phase of a spin texture acts as an emergent magnetic field on conduction electrons, producing the topological Hall effect and ultralow-current-driven motion. This established topological magnetism as a field spanning many materials and techniques, with prospects for low-power spintronic memory and logic.
